695.text:
Code of Conduct

		AG Open is dedicated to providing a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for everyone. If any guests or staff violates this code of conduct, the event organizers may take any action they deem appropriate, including expulsion from the event without refund and a ban from all future AG events.

We do not tolerate harassment or abuse of any kind. Harassment includes, but is not limited to, offensive language related to gender, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disability, religion (or lack thereof) or physical appearance, as well as deliberate intimidation, stalking, inappropriate physical contact, and unwelcome sexual attention.

Violations of safety include severely injuring another person due to an intentional action or neglecting to follow safety protocols given to you by staff, instructors. This Code of Conduct applies to all event spaces, affiliated venues, lodging areas, and any official or unofficial gatherings connected to AG Open, including online communication platforms.

Report violations to one of our lead staff immediately. Reports may be made to any staff member, tournament organizer, or through discord. All reports will be handled confidentially to the extent possible. Retaliation against anyone who reports a concern is strictly prohibited.

General  Sparring Tournament Rules

		This document provides the rules common to all tournaments. This is meant to serve as a minimum standard. Each tournament will have additional rules covering quality standards, scoring actions, and illegal actions. (With thanks to SoCal Swordfight, who's rules we were able to use as a starting point.)

Rules are subject to change up to the commencement of the tournament.

Changes from last year:

Moved penalty information that was spread across two sections into a single one that describes it more clearly.

Penalties for competitors who arrive to their matches with unacceptable equipment.

Clarified when a competitor is not "at fault" for a ring-out, and clarification that certain white cards can be called without being linked to a specific exchange.

Clarified definition of a throw.

Event Goals

Forbidden Actions

Match Conduct

Scoring Actions

Equipment

Event Goals

At a high level, the goal of AG Open tournaments is to showcase fencing which:

Displays good sportsmanship by everyone involved. If everyone isn’t having fun, then the event isn’t worth running.

Has a high level of competitive drive and promotes skill development and recognition.

Showcases historical techniques applied in a modern context.

Demonstrates a knowledge and familiarity with the use of sharp swords and high-quality striking mechanics.

Top of Page

Forbidden Actions

Any strike thrown with unrestrained force on the part of the attacker. Competitive martial arts fighting involves throwing forceful strikes with full intent to make contact, however each competitor is expected to maintain a respect for their opponent’s safety at all times. Should a safety issue arise, a fighter must do everything in their power to arrest their action in progress.

High amplitude throws,  joint locks, and leg wraps are prohibited in all tournaments. (Please refer to individual tournament rules to see if throws are permitted in any particular tournament.) A high amplitude throw is defined as any takedown action which either:

Raises the opponent’s hips above the level of their head in the execution.

Accelerates their opponent towards the ground, either through force and/or by lifting before releasing.

Directors WILL take into account the size difference between competitors when determining if sufficient control was demonstrated in a throw. If you are much larger than your opponent you are expected to be able to lower them down gently.

The ankle/foot is off target in all tournaments.

Exposing the spine or back of the head to the opponent. Note that if your opponent does expose such targets it is still your responsibility to do what you can to arrest the power of your strike.

Striking with a body part other than sword to deal percussive damage (punches, elbows, knees, headbutts, etc). 

Shoving using the arms/body is expected in close quarters. At lower tiers judges will consider size disparities as a potential cause for an excessive force penalty.

Actions will only be considered 'punches' if they are a clear deliberate blow thrown as a punch. Aggressive hand movements in a grapple which contact the mask are to be expected.

Raising your leg between you and your opponent to keep or expand separation is not a kick, so long as you don’t have a strong impact or deliver a violent shove.

Dangerous Action - Actions that director determines have created a dangerous situation, such as diving for a target with no intention of landing on your feet, or throwing yourself on the ground for any reason.

Things that everyone knows are banned everywhere, such as attacks with the hilt or throwing  anything.

Individual weapon tournaments may have additional rules in place. Be sure to read the rules for any tournaments you are entered in.

A dog may not participate in sword fighting matches.

Ring Outs

Should both of a fighter's feet leave the ring a hold will be called and they will receive a non-safety penalty for a ring out. Should a fighter ring out with such speed that they leave the immediate ring area they will receive a safety penalty.

Any action executed by a fencer who rings themselves out will "not have happened". Examples include:
Action: [A] hits [B] and runs out of the ring. Result: [A] gets no points for their attack, and is penalized 1 point.

Action: [A] hits [B]. [B] delivers an afterblow as [B] leaves ring. Result: [A] gets a clean hit, and [B] is penalized 1 point.

Action: [A] and [B] are wrestling at the edge of the ring, and [B] steps out of bounds. Result: [B] is penalized 1 point. (Don't wrestle at the edge of the ring to avoid this fate.)

This includes actions after the hold has been called. If you are running out of the ring after a hit has been delivered you will be penalized. (The director may exercise discretion if a fencer leave the ring for inadvertent actions such as de-tangling themselves from a grapple after hold.)

Top of Page

Match Conduct

All fighters will be expected to fight with both skill and control.

Fighters are expected to act professionally, and respectful to the officiating staff.

Fighters are expected to follow the commands of the tournament staff at all times.

This is a martial arts tournament and all fighters are expected to conduct themselves with respect for the weapon, their opponent, and the tournament staff. Any fighter that is deemed to pose a danger to themselves or others will be addressed at the discretion of the tournament director.

The tournament director will serve as the ultimate authority within the ring. The disciplinary procedure will generally constitute first a yellow card (warning), then a red card (penalty), then an expulsion from the match or tournament; however, it shall remain at the discretion of the director. Fighters who have been banned from attendance of previous AG Open tournaments, or from other major HEMA tournaments, must contact staff before attempting to register for any tournaments.

Fighters who have been banned from attendance of previous AG Open tournaments, or from other major HEMA tournaments, must contact staff before attempting to register for any tournaments.

Match End

Point Cap

 The point caps for tournaments are in the individual tournament rules.

Time Limit

Matches will run with the clock stopped between exchanges. At no point will a hold be called based on the clock expiring, and all time-outs will be based on the current time after the director has called for an exchange to end.

If no fighter reaches the point cap before 90 seconds the match will enter overtime. If a fencer in the lead is awarded a point after overtime begins they will win the match. However if they are unable to gain a point then the match will continue. (Aka if you are behind after 90 seconds you still have the potential for a comeback over multiple exchanges. If you are winning after 90 seconds you need to only score a single point to seal the deal.)

Should the clock exceed 150 seconds (2.5 min) at the conclusion of an exchange the match will hit the hard-cap and the fighter with the higher score will be declared the winner.
Ties are allowed in pool matches. If the fighters have the same score when past the normal time limit the match will end in a draw.

Longsword Relay has no time limit.

Examples ↓

Example: The score is 1-5 and [A] scores 3 points at 95 seconds into the match. The score is now 4-5 and the match continues until either: [A] is able to get ahead of [B], [B] is able to score a point, or the hard-cap is reached and [B] wins.

Example: The score is 4-4 and [B] scores 1 point on an exchange that ends at 92 seconds into the match. [B] has earned a go-ahead point after the soft-cap and wins the match 4-5.

Example: The score is 4-1 and the fighters double at 91 seconds into the match. The match continues. A second double is recorded at 103 seconds, and the match continues. [A] is able to score 2 points at 127 seconds and wins the match 6-2.

Self Calls

Fighters are able, and encouraged, to self-call attacks received; however, this is not required. A fighter who self-calls is only able to provide information to the match director, who may choose to use or discard the information as appropriate (e.g., if the attack was flat).
A fighter may only self-call in a manner which rewards their opponent. Valid self-calls are:

Indicating they were struck if judges missed the call.

Indicating they were struck in a higher value target than the judges are indicating.

Indicating that they did not strike the opponent.

Indicating that they struck the opponent in a lower value target than indicated.

If a fighter being awarded a clean hit self-calls a Double Hit the exchange will be recorded as a No Exchange.

If a fighter in a Double Hit calls their strike back it is up to the director if they will accept the self call or not, depending on their certainty of the original ruling.

Penalties

Penalties will be assessed as Safety or non-Safety. Any fighter who is awarded a penalty of either kind will have any scoring actions they performed that exchange invalidated*. (This means a double becomes a clean hit, etc)

Non-Safety Penalties (aka White Cards) are a -1 point deduction, and do not result in any escalation or disciplinary action.

Safety Penalties are escalating in nature, and follow the following escalation (the director may elect to skip steps in the case of egregious conduct):

Yellow Card - Warning

Red Card - Point deduction (3 points)

Black Card - Match forfeit. Automatic review for #4 by the tournament manager (don’t try to tempt fate, it’s basically a sure thing.)

Expulsion from the tournament

Safety penalties are tracked across the entire tournament. Repeating the same offence in a subsequent match will take into account the number of prior penalties of that offence.

*Should a director determine that a penalty occurred 'in-between' exchanges the white card may be applied without negating the scoring action on the last exchange. Examples are a fencer making an inappropriate remark after the score has been called and unrelated to the exchange, or a fencer leaving the ring while waiting for the judges to deliberate. (Running out of the ring after hold is still part of the prior exchange!)

Promptness

All fighters are expected to be ready to fight as soon as their match is called. This includes:

Being queued up behind their corner.

Having all their gear on.

Not being ready when your match is called will result in a penalty. It may only be a few seconds to you, but it adds up over hundreds of matches! Be courteous to everyone's time and be ready to start with no delays.

Bracket Advancement

After the conclusion of the pools the fighters/teams will be ranked by indicator score.  ALL fencers will advance to the elimination bracket.
Individual Tournaments

The top 50% will be advanced into the top half of a double elimination bracket, and the lower 50% will be advanced into the bottom half of a double elimination bracket. (This effectively means if you are in the top half of pool elims you have to lose twice to be eliminated, if you are in the bottom half you are eliminated after your first loss.) This will be a consolation style bracket, where if you are in the lower bracket the best you can do is bronze.

Grand Finals: The finals matches for Open LS-A, URG LS-A, and Relay will be held in the Grand Finals on Saturday afternoon. These matches will be a best-of-three format.

Normal Finals: For all other tournaments the finals will be a single match at the conclusion of their bracket.

Top of Page

Scoring Actions

Quality Standards

Points will be awarded for cuts/thrusts/slices/etc. in accordance with the rules of the individual tournaments. Scoring actions must display:

Deliberate intent and targeting on the part of the attacker.

Sufficient depth. Cuts with the tip of the sword or shallow thrusts are not scoring actions.

Example ↓

  Undeniably out of measure. While this is certainly hitting, we want purchase on the target.

Example ↓

  This is the 'ideal' amount of contact the judges are looking for, but as we know there is some wiggle room in practice.

Cuts

Cuts must be delivered with sufficient cutting plane, body structure, and blade arc.

Cutting plane is defined as the blade moving in line with a deliberate plane (edge alignment) and the sword moving along such a plane for the position of its movement immediately before striking the target. Special attention will be paid to horizontal strikes, as these typically display poor cutting plane and edge alignment.

Example (redirect) ↓

  Flat Hit  

Edge Hit, sword edge is brought on target and a cutting plane is generated. (Pause added for clarity).

Example (zwer) ↓

  Flat Hit  

Edge Hit

Example (torso) ↓

  Flat Hit  

Edge Hit

Sufficient body structure, which is not indicated by how hard the cut hits, but in demonstrating connection between the body and sword at the time of impact.

Example ↓

  Textbook good cut, arms are extended, the blade/crossguard are in line with the plane of motion on impact.

Example (hands) ↓

  No Structure, sword is flung on to hands by the flat. 

Well Structured, with body aligned with sword motion.

A sword must display rotation before contact with the target, typically in excess of 60 degrees. Rotation should not be considered the only determinant of quality, as some strikes may be acceptable given a very good cutting plane and body structure with shorter arc, and cuts with no structure/cutting plane will not be valid no matter how large the arc.

Example ↓

  Insufficient Cutting Plane, the sword is extended and just dropped to the target.  

Optimal Cutting Plane, could also be slightly smaller (but this is very difficult).

Example ↓

  A missed thrust brought onto the head is not a valid cut.

Thrusts

Thrusts must demonstrate the ability to penetrate into the target beyond a superficial depth. This can be demonstrated by a bend of the blade or visible force reaction at the point of contact. Should a fighter deliberately shorten the extension of their arm to lower the force of a thrust it will also be considered as a valid scoring action.

Example ↓

  A blade flex is not explicitly necessary, but easily communicates that the thrust had the required depth.

Example ↓

  You may also choose to shorten your step to soften the blow. This is still a valid scoring action, even though there is no flex.

Example ↓

  If you are stepping in deeply with your thrusts, it is expected that you relax your arms on impact.

Example ↓

  If you make light contact and are at full extension it is not a valid thrust.

Example ↓

  Chasing the opponent with the point touching is also not a valid thrust unless there is some pressure against the target.

Example ↓

  When in measure a thrust does not need to exert a lot of pressure, as the ability to achieve sufficient depth is clear.

It is understood that due to the design of HEMA masks a thrust to the mesh will have a high instance of being deflected on contact. It is further understood that the movement of a fighter may allow them to ‘roll out’ of contact from a thrust. A thrust that ‘glances off’ is a product of our protective gear, real sword points stick! (Though a thrust that misses and is pushed against the target with the flat is of course not valid, no matter how much the blade bends.)

Slices

Slices will only be considered as valid when performed against the upper opening and the arm (slices to the off-arm in 1h weapons do not count). The slice must show purposeful placement of the edge with sufficient force to display a clear reaction from the target. This may be demonstrated by pushing the target back at the point of contact, or simply preventing the target from being able to move freely. Drawing motion is not required, however note that this push requires a high degree of commitment, and is not simply sawing a blade back and forth on the body.

Example ↓

  Textbook slice driving up the blade. However, this is NOT the only way to have a slice qualify.

Example ↓

  So long as the blade is clearly inhibiting/interfering with the action of the arms it is a valid slice, even if there is no blade travel.

Example ↓

  Missing a thrust and then sawing is not a valid scoring action. Slices must show some force transfer between the sword and target. Either de-stabilizing your opponent, or interfering with their movement in some way. (Doesn't have to stop them in their tracks, but we should be able to see a reaction in their body.)

Example ↓

  Slices to the body are not valid scoring actions, no matter how much you sell it.

Pommel Strikes

Pommel strikes are only valid to the front of the mask and must demonstrate both deliberate action and control of force.

Pommel strikes do not need to make contact to be considered valid, provided there is an unambiguous path from the termination of the strike and the target.
Example ↓

  Both 1h and 2h are acceptable.

Example ↓

  Pommel strikes to the top or side of the mask are not scoring actions, and will incur a penalty if delivered deliberately and/or with force.

Pommel strikes which do make an impact must demonstrate control of force and respect for your opponent’s safety.
Example ↓

  Please don't do this

The motion of the sword must be in line with the pommel. Wildly pushing your sword hilt back and forth in a high bind does not constitute a pommel strike.
Example ↓

  While it wouldn't be pleasant to be on the receiving end, we want fighters to display a controlled and deliberate action. These are not valid scoring actions. (Doing the same thing, but harder, is also not appreciated.)

Targets

Target Area Definitions

“Upper opening”, for the purpose of these rules, includes both the head and cuts landing on the top of the torso, in an area from shoulder seam to shoulder seam. Should there be any lack of clarity if a blow struck the “upper opening” or arm target area a default of arm shall be taken - because you already missed the head by a wide margin.

Arm strikes will also include hand strikes. A strike to the handle of the sword will be considered as a strike to the hands. Note that full quality requirements are also in place for strikes to the hands.

Torso is the remaining area above the waist, Leg is below the waist. (Typically indicated by the bottom of the jacket.)

The foot/ankle is an illegal target in all tournaments

In the event of disagreement from the judges on the target area struck the point value will be decided at the discretion of the director.

Blade Grabs & Disarms

Disarms are (intentional or accidental) not scoring actions. A fighter must follow up a disarm with a valid scoring action. Should a fighter lose their weapon they may also concede a maximum point strike instead of attempting to enter distance for a grapple. (Running away is considered conceding.)

A blade may only be grabbed if it is not in motion, otherwise it will be counted as a scoring action to the hand. If the sword was in the process of attacking a high point value target, Target Substitution rules will apply. (Note: the director is always able to penalize any unsafe action, such as sticking the unprotected palm of the hand directly in the path of a strike.)

Target Substitution

If an arm is struck and 
It is not currently holding the sword,

The strike was likely to be a high value strike had it not hit the arm (cut/thrust head, thrust torso),

the attack will instead be registered against the higher value target. This is a point substitution, and not a warning/cardable offense.

Timing Of Actions

Double Hits

A double hit is defined as any time both fighters land valid scoring actions that were “in-flight” at the same time. It is possible for the hits to not be simultaneous, so long as the later hit was already moving forward when the first hit landed.

Example: [A] is circling their sword around to chamber when the strike from [B] lands, after which [B] swings the sword forward and strikes [A]. The attack from [B] was not started before they were struck, and it is not a double hit. (See the section on afterblows.)

Example: [A] see’s [B] circle their sword back to chamber, and launches an attack into the opening. By the time [A]’s strike lands the attack from [B] has already begun moving forward, and the attack from [B] lands shortly after. This is a double hit because both attacks were in flight at the same time. 

Example ↓

  They both hit each other at the same time. Double.

Example ↓

  Even though the attacks do not hit at the same time, they are in motion at the same time.

Example ↓

  This is stretching the definition of a double hit to the limit. There was no defensive reaction by the slower fighter, and both attacks were in flight at the same time.

Afterblow Definition

The afterblow is a valid scoring hit landing as the next action after a clean (aka non-double) hit. Any attack, step, or feint consumes the chance for an afterblow. An afterblow will deduct -1 from the point value of the initial attack’s score.

Example ↓

  This is and afterblow because the strike to the head follows the failed parry (hand hit)

Example ↓

  This is and afterblow because the strike to the hands is the next action instigated after being hit in the head.

Example ↓

  This is and afterblow because the initial clearing defensive action failed, and the cut to the head was a follow up.

Example ↓

  This is not a valid afterblow because it is two actions after the initial hit. (A feint and then a cut that lands.)

Example ↓

  This is not a valid afterblow. The first afterblow was blocked by the crossguard and the strike to the flank was the second attempt.

Pulling of Attacks

In just about all cases an attack that is “pulled” before it makes impact is not a valid scoring action. To be awarded points you must strike your opponent! (Though it is certainly considered good sportsmanship to strike as softly as possible when presented with an opening your opponent has no hope of defending.)

The exception to this rule is if their opponent has created an unsafe situation through their own actions (eg: expose back of the head, fall down). Should there be any risk to safety, for any reason, a fighter is expected to make every effort to pull back a strike in progress and/or not launch a strike to begin with. However, if a fighter can demonstrate they retained the wherewithal and capacity to launch an attack they will receive the maximum allowed point value for the exchange.

Note: Pommels strikes are an exception to this rule, and may be presented IF it is unambiguous that there is no obstacle to the target. (ie no hand in the way).

Example: A fighter turns the back of the head during an exchange and their opponent stops their blow in mid-flight. The fighter who was able to arrest their attack will be awarded points, and the fighter who exposed the target will be penalized.

Should a dangerous situation arise due to an action outside of the fighter's control (eg: gear failure) both fighters should immediately stop fighting and any actions delivered during or after the safety hold will not be valid scoring actions.

Example: A fighter’s elbow pad falls off and they hit their opponent in the next action. It will be assumed that their opponent was attempting to withdraw at the sight of the equipment failure, and therefore they were not fully committed to the fencing actions occurring.

Top of Page

Equipment

In the interest of promoting a professional HEMA image we do not allow heavy armor (breast plates, ect) or fantasy styled armors. In addition no protruding/dangling objects may be added on to tournament protective equipment or masks, except for those which are intended as safety modifications (i.e. addition of additional protective plates).  Any equipment which serves as a distraction to judges or participants (bells, inappropriate mask paint, etc) is not permitted. Disqualification of equipment rests at the discretion of the tournament manager, the event is under no obligation to allow you to use your custom or non-standard equipment.

All protective equipment and weapons must be inspected prior to competition. Swords, gloves, and masks must be checked at the gear check desk, and will be approved for the entire weekend. Other equipment will be inspected in the ring by the judging staff prior to the pool.
Should a competitor arrive to their match with unacceptable equipment they shall have a Non-Safety penalty applied for every piece of non-compliant equipment. This includes ill-fitting equipment such as leg protection which slides out of position on multiple occasions. (Director discretion shall be applied for things like equipment damage over the course of a match/tournament).

The following equipment is required for all sparring tournaments:

Masks with back of the head protection are required. (Back of head protectors which are are capable of sliding down are not acceptable. Example ↓)
This protector exposed the back of the head by not being affixed to the top of the mask.

)

Trachea protection that protects the throat from a direct thrust is required.

Heavy padded HEMA jacket.

Heavy HEMA Gloves (Sparring Gloves, SPES, Koning, ProGauntlets, Superior Fencing, Etc). Lacrosse & Red Dragon Gloves explicitly not allowed.

Testicle protection is required.

Rigid breast protection is recommended but not required.

Hard elbow protection.

Hard knee and shin protection.

Forearm protection is not required but recommended.

No exposed skin will be permitted.

If you are winning after 90 seconds you need to only score a single point to seal the deal.)

Should the clock exceed 150 seconds (2.5 min) at the conclusion of an exchange the match will hit the hard-cap and the fighter with the higher score will be declared the winner.

Ties are allowed in pool matches. If the fighters have the same score when past the normal time limit the match will end in a draw.

Longsword Relay has no time limit.

Examples ↓
  • Example: The score is 1-5 and [A] scores 3 points at 95 seconds into the match. The score is now 4-5 and the match continues until either: [A] is able to get ahead of [B], [B] is able to score a point, or the hard-cap is reached and [B] wins.
  • Example: The score is 4-4 and [B] scores 1 point on an exchange that ends at 92 seconds into the match. [B] has earned a go-ahead point after the soft-cap and wins the match 4-5.
  • Example: The score is 4-1 and the fighters double at 91 seconds into the match. The match continues. A second double is recorded at 103 seconds, and the match continues. [A] is able to score 2 points at 127 seconds and wins the match 6-2.

Self Calls

Fighters are able, and encouraged, to self-call attacks received; however, this is not required. A fighter who self-calls is only able to provide information to the match director, who may choose to use or discard the information as appropriate (e.g., if the attack was flat). A fighter may only self-call in a manner which rewards their opponent. Valid self-calls are:

  • Indicating they were struck if judges missed the call.
  • Indicating they were struck in a higher value target than the judges are indicating.
  • Indicating that they did not strike the opponent.
  • Indicating that they struck the opponent in a lower value target than indicated.
  • If a fighter being awarded a clean hit self-calls a Double Hit the exchange will be recorded as a No Exchange.
  • If a fighter in a Double Hit calls their strike back it is up to the director if they will accept the self call or not, depending on their certainty of the original ruling.

Penalties

Penalties will be assessed as Safety or non-Safety. Any fighter who is awarded a penalty of either kind will have any scoring actions they performed that exchange invalidated*. (This means a double becomes a clean hit, etc)

Non-Safety Penalties (aka White Cards) are a -1 point deduction, and do not result in any escalation or disciplinary action.

Safety Penalties are escalating in nature, and follow the following escalation (the director may elect to skip steps in the case of egregious conduct):

  1. Yellow Card - Warning
  2. Red Card - Point deduction (3 points)
  3. Black Card - Match forfeit. Automatic review for #4 by the tournament manager (don’t try to tempt fate, it’s basically a sure thing.)
  4. Expulsion from the tournament

Safety penalties are tracked across the entire tournament. Repeating the same offence in a subsequent match will take into account the number of prior penalties of that offence.
*Should a director determine that a penalty occurred 'in-between' exchanges the white card may be applied without negating the scoring action on the last exchange. Examples are a fencer making an inappropriate remark after the score has been called and unrelated to the exchange, or a fencer leaving the ring while waiting for the judges to deliberate. (Running out of the ring after hold is still part of the prior exchange!)

Promptness

All fighters are expected to be ready to fight as soon as their match is called. This includes:

  • Being queued up behind their corner.
  • Having all their gear on.

Not being ready when your match is called will result in a penalty. It may only be a few seconds to you, but it adds up over hundreds of matches! Be courteous to everyone's time and be ready to start with no delays.

Bracket Advancement

After the conclusion of the pools the fighters/teams will be ranked by indicator score. ALL fencers will advance to the elimination bracket.

Individual Tournaments

The top 50% will be advanced into the top half of a double elimination bracket, and the lower 50% will be advanced into the bottom half of a double elimination bracket. (This effectively means if you are in the top half of pool elims you have to lose twice to be eliminated, if you are in the bottom half you are eliminated after your first loss.) This will be a consolation style bracket, where if you are in the lower bracket the best you can do is bronze.
Grand Finals: The finals matches for Open LS-A, URG LS-A, and Relay will be held in the Grand Finals on Saturday afternoon. These matches will be a best-of-three format.
Normal Finals: For all other tournaments the finals will be a single match at the conclusion of their bracket.

Top of Page

Scoring Actions

Quality Standards

Points will be awarded for cuts/thrusts/slices/etc. in accordance with the rules of the individual tournaments. Scoring actions must display:

  1. Deliberate intent and targeting on the part of the attacker.
  2. Sufficient depth. Cuts with the tip of the sword or shallow thrusts are not scoring actions.
    Example ↓
    Undeniably out of measure. While this is certainly hitting, we want purchase on the target.
    3. Example ↓
    This is the 'ideal' amount of contact the judges are looking for, but as we know there is some wiggle room in practice.

Cuts

Cuts must be delivered with sufficient cutting plane, body structure, and blade arc.

  • Cutting plane is defined as the blade moving in line with a deliberate plane (edge alignment) and the sword moving along such a plane for the position of its movement immediately before striking the target. Special attention will be paid to horizontal strikes, as these typically display poor cutting plane and edge alignment.
    Example (redirect) ↓
    Flat Hit


    Edge Hit, sword edge is brought on target and a cutting plane is generated. (Pause added for clarity).
    Example (zwer) ↓
    Flat Hit


    Edge Hit
    Example (torso) ↓
    Flat Hit


    Edge Hit
  • Sufficient body structure, which is not indicated by how hard the cut hits, but in demonstrating connection between the body and sword at the time of impact.
    Example ↓
    Textbook good cut, arms are extended, the blade/crossguard are in line with the plane of motion on impact.
    Example (hands) ↓
    No Structure, sword is flung on to hands by the flat.


    Well Structured, with body aligned with sword motion.
  • A sword must display rotation before contact with the target, typically in excess of 60 degrees. Rotation should not be considered the only determinant of quality, as some strikes may be acceptable given a very good cutting plane and body structure with shorter arc, and cuts with no structure/cutting plane will not be valid no matter how large the arc.
    Example ↓
    Insufficient Cutting Plane, the sword is extended and just dropped to the target.


    Optimal Cutting Plane, could also be slightly smaller (but this is very difficult).
    Example ↓
    A missed thrust brought onto the head is not a valid cut.

Thrusts

Thrusts must demonstrate the ability to penetrate into the target beyond a superficial depth. This can be demonstrated by a bend of the blade or visible force reaction at the point of contact. Should a fighter deliberately shorten the extension of their arm to lower the force of a thrust it will also be considered as a valid scoring action.

  • Example ↓
    A blade flex is not explicitly necessary, but easily communicates that the thrust had the required depth.
  • Example ↓
    You may also choose to shorten your step to soften the blow. This is still a valid scoring action, even though there is no flex.
  • Example ↓
    If you are stepping in deeply with your thrusts, it is expected that you relax your arms on impact.
  • Example ↓
    If you make light contact and are at full extension it is not a valid thrust.
  • Example ↓
    Chasing the opponent with the point touching is also not a valid thrust unless there is some pressure against the target.
  • Example ↓
    When in measure a thrust does not need to exert a lot of pressure, as the ability to achieve sufficient depth is clear.

It is understood that due to the design of HEMA masks a thrust to the mesh will have a high instance of being deflected on contact. It is further understood that the movement of a fighter may allow them to ‘roll out’ of contact from a thrust. A thrust that ‘glances off’ is a product of our protective gear, real sword points stick! (Though a thrust that misses and is pushed against the target with the flat is of course not valid, no matter how much the blade bends.)

Slices

Slices will only be considered as valid when performed against the upper opening and the arm (slices to the off-arm in 1h weapons do not count). The slice must show purposeful placement of the edge with sufficient force to display a clear reaction from the target. This may be demonstrated by pushing the target back at the point of contact, or simply preventing the target from being able to move freely. Drawing motion is not required, however note that this push requires a high degree of commitment, and is not simply sawing a blade back and forth on the body.

  • Example ↓
    Textbook slice driving up the blade. However, this is NOT the only way to have a slice qualify.
  • Example ↓
    So long as the blade is clearly inhibiting/interfering with the action of the arms it is a valid slice, even if there is no blade travel.
  • Example ↓
    Missing a thrust and then sawing is not a valid scoring action. Slices must show some force transfer between the sword and target. Either de-stabilizing your opponent, or interfering with their movement in some way. (Doesn't have to stop them in their tracks, but we should be able to see a reaction in their body.)
  • Example ↓
    Slices to the body are not valid scoring actions, no matter how much you sell it.

Pommel Strikes

Pommel strikes are only valid to the front of the mask and must demonstrate both deliberate action and control of force.

  • Pommel strikes do not need to make contact to be considered valid, provided there is an unambiguous path from the termination of the strike and the target. Example ↓
    Both 1h and 2h are acceptable.
    Example ↓
    Pommel strikes to the top or side of the mask are not scoring actions, and will incur a penalty if delivered deliberately and/or with force.
  • Pommel strikes which do make an impact must demonstrate control of force and respect for your opponent’s safety. Example ↓
    Please don't do this
  • The motion of the sword must be in line with the pommel. Wildly pushing your sword hilt back and forth in a high bind does not constitute a pommel strike. Example ↓
    While it wouldn't be pleasant to be on the receiving end, we want fighters to display a controlled and deliberate action. These are not valid scoring actions. (Doing the same thing, but harder, is also not appreciated.)

Targets

Target Area Definitions

“Upper opening”, for the purpose of these rules, includes both the head and cuts landing on the top of the torso, in an area from shoulder seam to shoulder seam. Should there be any lack of clarity if a blow struck the “upper opening” or arm target area a default of arm shall be taken - because you already missed the head by a wide margin.

Arm strikes will also include hand strikes. A strike to the handle of the sword will be considered as a strike to the hands. Note that full quality requirements are also in place for strikes to the hands.

Torso is the remaining area above the waist, Leg is below the waist. (Typically indicated by the bottom of the jacket.)

The foot/ankle is an illegal target in all tournaments

Disarms are (intentional or accidental) not scoring actions. A fighter must follow up a disarm with a valid scoring action. Should a fighter lose their weapon they may also concede a maximum point strike instead of attempting to enter distance for a grapple. (Running away is considered conceding.)

A blade may only be grabbed if it is not in motion, otherwise it will be counted as a scoring action to the hand. If the sword was in the process of attacking a high point value target, Target Substitution rules will apply. (Note: the director is always able to penalize any unsafe action, such as sticking the unprotected palm of the hand directly in the path of a strike.)

Target Substitution

If an arm is struck and

  1. It is not currently holding the sword,
  2. The strike was likely to be a high value strike had it not hit the arm (cut/thrust head, thrust torso),
the attack will instead be registered against the higher value target. This is a point substitution, and not a warning/cardable offense.

Timing Of Actions

Double Hits

A double hit is defined as any time both fighters land valid scoring actions that were “in-flight” at the same time. It is possible for the hits to not be simultaneous, so long as the later hit was already moving forward when the first hit landed.

  • Example: [A] is circling their sword around to chamber when the strike from [B] lands, after which [B] swings the sword forward and strikes [A]. The attack from [B] was not started before they were struck, and it is not a double hit. (See the section on afterblows.)
  • Example: [A] see’s [B] circle their sword back to chamber, and launches an attack into the opening. By the time [A]’s strike lands the attack from [B] has already begun moving forward, and the attack from [B] lands shortly after. This is a double hit because both attacks were in flight at the same time.
  • Example ↓
    They both hit each other at the same time. Double.
  • Example ↓
    Even though the attacks do not hit at the same time, they are in motion at the same time.
  • Example ↓
    This is stretching the definition of a double hit to the limit. There was no defensive reaction by the slower fighter, and both attacks were in flight at the same time.

Afterblow Definition

The afterblow is a valid scoring hit landing as the next action after a clean (aka non-double) hit. Any attack, step, or feint consumes the chance for an afterblow. An afterblow will deduct -1 from the point value of the initial attack’s score.

  • Example ↓
    This is and afterblow because the strike to the head follows the failed parry (hand hit)
  • Example ↓
    This is and afterblow because the strike to the hands is the next action instigated after being hit in the head.
  • Example ↓
    This is and afterblow because the initial clearing defensive action failed, and the cut to the head was a follow up.
  • Example ↓
    This is not a valid afterblow because it is two actions after the initial hit. (A feint and then a cut that lands.)
  • Example ↓
    This is not a valid afterblow. The first afterblow was blocked by the crossguard and the strike to the flank was the second attempt.

Pulling of Attacks

In just about all cases an attack that is “pulled” before it makes impact is not a valid scoring action. To be awarded points you must strike your opponent! (Though it is certainly considered good sportsmanship to strike as softly as possible when presented with an opening your opponent has no hope of defending.)

The exception to this rule is if their opponent has created an unsafe situation through their own actions (eg: expose back of the head, fall down). Should there be any risk to safety, for any reason, a fighter is expected to make every effort to pull back a strike in progress and/or not launch a strike to begin with. However, if a fighter can demonstrate they retained the wherewithal and capacity to launch an attack they will receive the maximum allowed point value for the exchange.

Note: Pommels strikes are an exception to this rule, and may be presented IF it is unambiguous that there is no obstacle to the target. (ie no hand in the way).

  • Example: A fighter turns the back of the head during an exchange and their opponent stops their blow in mid-flight. The fighter who was able to arrest their attack will be awarded points, and the fighter who exposed the target will be penalized.

Should a dangerous situation arise due to an action outside of the fighter's control (eg: gear failure) both fighters should immediately stop fighting and any actions delivered during or after the safety hold will not be valid scoring actions.

  • Example: A fighter’s elbow pad falls off and they hit their opponent in the next action. It will be assumed that their opponent was attempting to withdraw at the sight of the equipment failure, and therefore they were not fully committed to the fencing actions occurring.

Top of Page

Equipment

In the interest of promoting a professional HEMA image we do not allow heavy armor (breast plates, ect) or fantasy styled armors. In addition no protruding/dangling objects may be added on to tournament protective equipment or masks, except for those which are intended as safety modifications (i.e. addition of additional protective plates). Any equipment which serves as a distraction to judges or participants (bells, inappropriate mask paint, etc) is not permitted. Disqualification of equipment rests at the discretion of the tournament manager, the event is under no obligation to allow you to use your custom or non-standard equipment.

All protective equipment and weapons must be inspected prior to competition. Swords, gloves, and masks must be checked at the gear check desk, and will be approved for the entire weekend. Other equipment will be inspected in the ring by the judging staff prior to the pool.

Should a competitor arrive to their match with unacceptable equipment they shall have a Non-Safety penalty applied for every piece of non-compliant equipment. This includes ill-fitting equipment such as leg protection which slides out of position on multiple occasions. (Director discretion shall be applied for things like equipment damage over the course of a match/tournament).

The following equipment is required for all sparring tournaments:

  • Masks with back of the head protection are required. (Back of head protectors which are are capable of sliding down are not acceptable. Example ↓)
    This protector exposed the back of the head by not being affixed to the top of the mask.
    )
  • Trachea protection that protects the throat from a direct thrust is required.
  • Heavy padded HEMA jacket.
  • Heavy HEMA Gloves (Sparring Gloves, SPES, Koning, ProGauntlets, Superior Fencing, Etc). Lacrosse & Red Dragon Gloves explicitly not allowed.
  • Testicle protection is required.
  • Rigid breast protection is recommended but not required.
  • Hard elbow protection.
  • Hard knee and shin protection.
  • Forearm protection is not required but recommended.
  • No exposed skin will be permitted.

Top of Page

697.text:
Longsword Individual Rules

		This document provides the rules specific to the Longsword Tournaments. All rules outlined in the General Tournament Standards also apply to the longsword tournaments, and offer more depth on the criteria for scoring actions.

Rules are subject to change up to the commencement of the tournament.

Changes from last year:

Max blade length lowered from 102 cm to 101 cm.

Max blade flex lowered from 19.5 kg to 18 kg. (Measured at the cross).

Tournament Goal

The goal of the Longsword tournament is to both showcase and help develop skill in utilizing the longsword for the purpose of unarmored combat, as outlined by the KdF tradition. (Of course, all other traditions are invited to play!) This includes the use of the longsword as a sharp sword. Tournament rules and judging standards are meant to advance fundamental skills, such as integrating cutting mechanics into antagonistic sparring. A match is not a simulation of a sword duel.

In the use of a longsword there are times when you would wish to use more or less debilitating striking mechanics, but if you don’t demonstrate high quality strikes when asked to, it shows you are not capable of them. It is the goal of AG Open to stress test high quality striking interpretations and push the fighters to achieve these. There are many other existing venues which test a fencer's skill and ability to achieve touches as quickly as possible.

AG Open will seed fighters into appropriate tournament tier based on results of past longsword tournaments, with the aim of creating as many meaningful matches as possible. (aka matches where you are close in skill to your opponent.)

Illegal Actions

All illegal actions from the General Tournament Rules apply to this tournament, including but not limited to: lack of control/excessive force, high amplitude throws, or anything else that has a high chance to hurt somebody. Refer to the General Tournament Rules for more details.

Exposing the spine or back of the head to the opponent. Note that if your opponent does expose such targets it is still your responsibility to do what you can to arrest the power of your strike.

Should a fighter execute one handed blows outside of the grapple they may be  awarded a non-safety penalty for unsporting conduct  (-1 pt) at the discretion of the director.

Scoring Actions

Matches will be fought until a fighter reaches a score of 10 points.

3 pts: Cut or Thrust to Upper Opening

3 pts: Thrust to Torso over Sword Hilt/Arms*

2 pts: All other Cuts & Thrusts. Also Slices to the arms or Upper Opening. 
*Thrusts constraining over the blade will be considered "over the sword". ie mutieren or winding against ochs.

*Controlling the opponent's sword in a grapple is also considered "over the sword".

Examples ↓

  YES Textbook thrust over the sword.

YES This is low on the torso, but still over the sword.

NO This is at the same height as above, but is below the opponent's arms and sword.

NO This is high, but the sword is higher. (Note that a thrust to the mask is still always 3 points regardless of under/over.)

YES The target is low, but the blade is engaged above the opponent's sword.

YES The sword is below the arms, but it is part of a grapple.

Additional Scoring Actions:

Pommel Strike to Mask	1 pt

Standing Takedown		3 pts

Afterblow and Double Hits will be scored in accordance with the General Tournament Rules. (Afterblow is -1 from initial score. Don’t double.)

One-handed strikes are not permitted except when the hand is removed as part of a grappling technique executed against an opponent.

Double Hits

Double Hits are recorded as no match score for each fighter, and are factored into the overall indicator score for the pools. There is an increasing negative score for each double hit, cumulative over the entire pool. (-1/-2/-3/ etc). If 3 double hits are recorded in a pool match it shall end without a winner.

If a double hit is very obviously the result of one party blatantly ignoring the threat of the opponent’s weapon an additional 1 point non-safety penalty  will be assessed to this fighter. (But it’s still a double.)
Example: Attacks to the lower torso or legs when the opponent is chambered to cut to the upper opening.

Wrestling and Takedowns

The amount of time permitted for a wrestling action is a 5-count from the director; beginning when both of the swords are inhibited (discarded, entangled, etc). This count may or may not be verbalized at the director's discretion.

A standing takedown is a wrestling action that deliberately and safely brings a part of opponent other than the feet/knees to the ground, while the throwing fighter remains standing.  Standing requires one foot remain on the ground, dropping to a single knee is acceptable.

Tournament Format

Match Length

Point Cap in Pools: 7 pts

Point Cap in Elims: 10 pts

Time Limit: 90 seconds, with 60 seconds possible overtime

Bracket Advancement

All fighters will advance to a double elimination bracket. The top 1/2 of ranked fencers will advance to the upper bracket and the bottom 1/2 of ranked fencers will advance directly to the lower bracket, as if they already have had one loss.

Equipment

All protective equipment and weapons must be inspected prior to competition. A fighter must show up to gear check wearing their equipment.

Protective Equipment

All equipment from the General Tournament Standards is required.

Weapons

The following are the expectations for the swords used in the AG Open Lonsword Tournaments. Developing formal equipment standards for HEMA is a work in progress, and the tournament manager's judgement day-off will serve as the ultimate authority for any case not sufficiently captured in these requirements.

1) A 'standard' straight bladed longsword feder is expected ("shiltless feders" designed for high intensity sparring are also permitted. Thin edged 'blunts' are not.).

2) Ring hilts or other hand protection over and above a straight crossguard are not permitted.

3) The point must have an expanded surface area, or be affixed with a tip of some sort.

4) Blades must be free of any large burs or hilt protrusions which may cause a risk to an opponent's safety or their equipment.

5) Sword measurements are expected to fall within these ranges:

Blade Length: 84 - 101 cm (33 - 40")

Sword Mass: 1.3 - 1.8 kg (2.9 - 3.9 lbs. )

Buckling Strength: 10 - 18 kg (How is this measured?)

6) Be manufactured by a known HEMA equipment supplier.

698.name: Longsword Relay Rules
698.text:
Longsword Relay Rules

		This document provides the rules specific to the Longsword Relay Tournament. All rules outlined in the General Tournament Rules also apply to the relay tournament.

Rules are subject to change up to the commencement of the tournament.

Changes from last year:

Open Relay has now been split into Tier-A and Tier-B.

URG Relay this year! 🥳

Tournament Goal

The goal of the team longsword tournament is to promote school spirit and healthy competition between groups, rather than just between individuals. This is a serious tournament, and the centerpiece of the event. We are expecting fencers to be competing as intensely for their school team as they would in the individual longsword tournaments.  

Team Composition

A team is composed of three individuals from the same school/club. Mixed school/club team entries are not allowed. Prior to the commencement of the tournament we will gather all individuals with no team who wish to compete, and form teams for Tier-B randomly from this pool.

Teams are expected to self-sort according to have their weakest member be first in the order and their strongest member last. (AGO reserves the right to determine the fighter order of teams.)

699.name: Messer Rules
699.text:
Messer Rules

		This document provides the rules specific to the messer tournament. All rules outlined in the General Tournament Standards also apply to the messer tournament, and offer more depth on the criteria for scoring actions.

Rules are subject to change up to the commencement of the tournament.

Changes from last year:

Buckling flex limit reduced to 19.5 kg.

Clarified pommels are non-scoring.

Tournament Goal

The goal of the Messer sword tournament is to both showcase and develop skill in utilizing the messer for the purpose of unarmored combat, as outlined by the KdF tradition. (Of course all other traditions are invited to play!) This includes the use of the sword as a sharp sword and close quarters fencing. Tournament rules and judging standards are meant to advance fundamental skills, such as integrating cutting mechanics into antagonistic sparring. A match is not a simulation of a sword duel.

In the use of a sword there are times when you would wish to use more or less debilitating striking mechanics, but if you don't demonstrate high quality strikes when asked to, it shows you are not capable of them. It is the goal of AG Open to stress test high quality striking interpretations and push the fighters to achieve these. There are many other existing venues which test a fencer's skill and ability to achieve touches as quickly as possible.

Illegal Actions

All illegal actions from the General Tournament Rules apply to this tournament, including but not limited to: lack of control/excessive force, high amplitude throws, or anything else that has a high chance to hurt somebody. Refer to the General Tournament Rules for more details.

Exposing the spine or back of the head to the opponent. Note that if your opponent does expose such targets it is still your responsibility to do what you can to arrest the power of your strike.

Scoring Actions

Matches will be fought until a fighter reaches a score of 7 points.

2 pts: Clean Hit* or Standing Takedown

 * Each competitor will only have their first 3 shallow target hits count as scoring actions. 

* Double hits to a shallow target will also count towards one of the 3 shallow target hits.

* Deep = upper opening or a thrust to the torso. Everything else is shallow.

1 pts: Technical Clean**

 ** If there is a double where one competitor hits a scoring target and one hits a non-scoring target it will be a technical clean and award 1 point.

Pommel strikes are non-scoring in messer.

Examples ↓

Example 1
A hits shallow :		+2 A, 2 shallow hits remain

A hits deep :		       +2 A, 2 shallow hits remain

A hits shallow :		+2 A, 1 shallow hit remains

A hits shallow :		+2 A, 0 shallow hit remains (A hits point cap and wins)

Example 2
A hits shallow :		+2 A, 2 shallow hits remain

A hits deep :		+2 A, 2 shallow hits remain

A shallow, B deep :	No points, 1 shallow hit remains for A

A shallow :		+2 A, 0 shallow hits remain

A shallow :		No points as no more shallow hits remain.

A shallow, B deep :	+1 B, since it is a technical clean

A shallow, B shallow :	+1 B, since B has shallows left it is a valid hit and a technical clean

A shallow, B shallow :	+1 B, since B has shallows left it is a valid hit and a technical clean

B shallow :		+2 B, B has no more shallow hits

A shallow, B shallow :	No points, both have used up their shallows

A deep, B shallow :	+1 A, technical clean

Match Length

Point Cap : 7 pts

Time Limit: 90 seconds, with 60 seconds possible overtime. Each exchange will add a minimum of 10 seconds to the clock

Equipment

All protective equipment and weapons must be inspected prior to competition. A fighter must show up to gear check wearing their equipment.

Protective Equipment

All equipment from the General Tournament Standards is required.

Weapons

The following are the expectations for the swords used in the AG Messer Tournaments. Developing formal equipment standards for HEMA is a work in progress, and the tournament manager's judgement day-off will serve as the ultimate authority for any case not sufficiently captured in these requirements.

1) A 'standard' straight bladed messer is expected. (Yes, we are aware the leading edge of a standard messer has a curve to it.)

2) Messers must have a crossguard and a nagel (or nagel like protrusion). Any other hand protection (knucklebow, etc) is not permitted.

3) The point must have an expanded surface area, or be affixed with a tip of some sort.

4) Blades must be free of any large burs or protrusions which may cause a risk to an opponent's safety or their equipment.

5) Sword measurements are expected to fall within these ranges:

Blade Length: less than  74 cm (29")

Buckling Strength: 10 - 19.5 kg (How is this measured?)

6) Be manufactured by a known HEMA equipment supplier.

700.name: Longsword Cutting Rules
700.text:
Longsword Cutting Rules

Tournament Goals

Equipment

Static (Tier B) Cutting Patterns

Dynamic (Tier A) Cutting Patterns

Quality Standards

Competitor Conduct

Rules are subject to change up to the commencement of the tournament.

Changes from last year:

None

Tournament Goals

The goal of the AG Open cutting tournaments is to:

Showcase/evaluate/reward sword skills that can not be tested in a sparring environment.

Promote an integrated training regiment, with good cutting mechanics in sparring and good fencing behavior in cutting

Be creative, educational, and enjoyable for both participants and spectators.

Top of Page

Equipment

The AG Open Longsword Cutting tournaments will be performed using unsharpened "sharp" longswords which will be provided by the tournament.
These are not sharp, but have edges which are very thin and are considerably easier to cut with than any feder paper cutting you may have seen in the past. Though there are not any safety procedures associated with sharp swords, please be aware it is still a steel bar and can hurt someone if handled recklessly.

Top of Page

Static (Tier B) Cutting Patterns

Seeding: Solo Cuts

Competitors will complete a cutting pattern and be advanced to the elimination based on their score. (Like doing pools in a sparring tournament.)

Target 1: Competitors will perform 3 descending cuts from the right side on a single pull of hanging paper.

Target 2: Competitors will perform 3 descending cuts from the left side on a single pull of hanging paper.

Target 3: Competitors will perform 3 ascending cuts from the either side on a single pull of hanging paper.

Eliminations

Competitors will be seeded into a finals bracket based on the first round, in the same style as the sparring tournaments. Number of advancing competitors will be based on tournament size.

Cutting Patterns TBA

Top of Page

Dynamic (Tier-A) Cutting Patterns

Seeding Round: Lateral Sprints

The competitor will have 60 seconds to score as my points as possible by moving between and cutting at two cutting stands placed a distance apart. The competitor may perform as many cuts as they want on a stand (each cut will be scored for quality), until they have insufficient amount of paper remaining. The paper will be reset while the competitor is cutting on the opposite target. 
Cuts must be descending cuts, away from the center. (See the example.)

Example ↓ 

    Image is obviously not to scale.

Eliminations

Competitors will be seeded into a finals bracket based on the first round, in the same style as the sparring tournaments.

Cutting Patterns TBA

Top of Page

Quality Standards

Paper cutting will be performed on a vertical hanging paper. Points will be awarded as follows:

[+4 pts]: Clean Cut 

[+3 pts]: Minor Roughness Example ↓

[+3 pts]: Minor Paper Flutter

[+2 pts]: Small Rip Example ↓

[+2 pts]: Small Scallop Example ↓

[+2 pts]: Sound of impact or strong paper flutter

[0 pts]: Ripped Paper Example ↓

[0 pts]: Large Scallop Example ↓

Top of Page

Competitor Conduct

Competitors shall not begin cutting until instructed to do so by the tournament staff. For static cutting rounds the competitor must wait for confirmation from the cutting judges before beginning their next cut, or it may not be scored.

Competitors that take excessive time  to begin after they have been signaled to cut will be warned by the tournament staff, and may be subject to penalties if there are repeated infractions. While it is not necessary for a competitor to rush after they are prompted, it is intended that they perform the cut in a short period of time without spending considerable time ‘fidgeting’ or ‘psyching themselves up.’

Top of Page

701.name: Aggregate Team Award
701.text:
Aggregate Team Award

		Tournament Goal

The Aggregate Team Award is meant to highlight the groups who attend AG Open with a team showcasing both:

Performance: Ability to make it to the top of the tournaments.

Depth: The combined performance of the school as a whole, rather than a single stand-out individual of the school.

Scoring

Each individual will have their best result considered, and their points added to their team's score.

Top 4 of tournament (finalist): 9 points

Top 1/3 of tournament: 3 points

Top 1/2 of tournament: 1 point

The Team Aggregate score is the sum of all of the team member's contributions. Bringing more people to the event is always a good thing. 🙂

Note: Each individual is counted once. If you win 3 gold medals you are a pretty awesome individual and having a fantastic weekend. But still only contribute 9 points to your team.

(An individual's Longsword Relay result does count towards the Aggregate Team Score, unless the individual is on one of the mixed school pickup teams, or on a school team that has elected to compete in Tier-B)
